title: Lil’ Rent
text: Welcome back to Wake Up Denver's Early Bird Hour. I'm Sam Dockman. Our field correspondent, Janet Veit, is at the Youth Theatre Works Playhouse in downtown Denver where a big show is in the works. Janet, what's going on? Well, Sam, I'm here at rehearsal with some of Denver's most talented young thespians. Oh, thespians rhymes with lesbians. Hubba hubba. I don't like that. Take them off the split screen. The cast of Denver Youth Theatre Works' annual spring musical is hard at work on their new show, and there's about 525,600 reasons to see Lil' Rent, which opens Thursday. I'm joined now by the very busy director, Lowell Dubbins. Oh, hi. Sorry. It is a madhouse hello. We're in the middle of Hell Week, which is living up to its name. Lowell, so tell us about the show. All right. Lil' Rent is an abridged, family-friendly version of the hit musical about New York City artists living through the HIV-AIDS crisis of the late 80s. Now, and how does Lil' Rent handle the intense HIV-AIDS subject matter with a cast of children? Right. In Lil' Rent, HIV-AIDS is changed to diabetes. And, um, it really doesn't change things at all. Really? It's just that in the original, HIV-AIDS is, like, that's what Rent's about. You know, characters die from it. So how did you go about changing the original script? Well, I used the find and replace feature in Microsoft Word and replaced it with, like, just HIV-AIDS with diabetes. Okay. And I honestly think it's more powerful this way. Well, I... You're going to love it. I don't know about that, but, um, let's meet some of the cast here. Oh, yes. This is the brilliant Sean Kessler, who plays Mark, and you may have seen him in Last Fall's Lil' Equus. It is Nathan Benson, who plays Roger. My goodness. So, okay, I understand you're going to be doing a little scene for us. Uh, yes, ma'am. This is a scene from Act 1, where my character is singing about his friend Roger, who is diabetes-positive. Mm-hmm. And in the late 80s, when the show takes place, diabetes was this new sexually transmitted disease that people didn't know a lot about. It was scary. Yeah. Back then, diabetes was basically a death sentence. Oh, well, it wasn't, but go ahead. Yes, yes. They say diabetes is a gay disease, but Roger got diabetes from having sex with his girlfriend. Close on Roger, whose girlfriend left him a note saying, we've got diabetes, before slitting her wrists in the bathroom. Take your insulin, Roger. And scene. Very powerful, boys. Ooh. Okay, well, let's meet more of the cast. Yes. This is Amy Meriwether Sherman, another rising star. She's incredibly talented, and fiercely conservative. Yeah, hello, my name is Amy Meriwether Sherman, and I am this many years old. My favorite political party is the Republicans, and my favorite book is Liar in Chink, How Obama Killed the Middle Class. And also, A Million Bedillion Goes Camping. Okay, wow, a lot to take in there. Who are you playing? Well, ma'am, I play Mimi Vasquez. She's a Puerto Rican stripper and a heroin addict. Who got diabetes from sharing an infected hair and needle. All right, remember, we say dancer, not stripper. But she takes her clothes off. Okay. Uh, tell them about, uh... Tell them about your Spanish. Your Spanish. Oh, yes, okay. So, ma'am, I learned some Spanish to play Mimi because she only speaks Spanish, and I only speak white. But... the way you say diabetes in Spanish is Diabeetos. Oh, okay. All right, well, how about we get to that song? Yes, Amy will be performing an excerpt from her big solo, Out Tonight. This song is about my character. It's horny, and she wants to go find someone to have sex with. Let's go A-U tonight. I'm a Puerto Rican stripper, and I want to go out tonight. Meow. And scene.
